title: The World’s Largest Penguin Colony Suffers Catastrophic Loss - Nautilus
author: Devin Reese
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentThe World’s Largest Penguin Colony Suffers Catastrophic LossSomething is amiss in AntarcticaDRBy Devin Reese12:00 PM CDT on October 21, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIn 2000, a doctoral student from Stony Brook University reported that chinstrap penguins (Pygoscelis antarcticus) on the Antarctica peninsula were on the decline. But without solid baseline numbers for their stronghold in the South Sandwich Archipelago, he couldn’t assess the magnitude of the decline. A recently published study in the journal Cell, however, has now made it abundantly clear: The populations of chinstraps on Zavadoski Island, which boasted the largest penguin colony in the world, have dramatically collapsed over the last 15 years.Biologists from the U.K., U.S., Germany, South Africa, and Chile used drone surveys and aerial photos, along with satellite images that detect patches of penguin poop, to estimate penguin population sizes on the island. The data showed that chinstrap numbers plummeted from more than 500,000 individuals in 2011 to about 200,000 by 2025. On the other hand, macaroni penguins (Eudyptes chrysolophus), which also inhabit Zavodovski, increased in number by almost 30 percent—from an estimated 90,000 to more than 200,000.Read more: “My Life with the Penguins”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
